To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hybridization number, the rSPR and TBR distance are fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the minimum level of phylogenetic networks displaying both trees.

the cluster reduction rule can transform any $$O(n^{f(p)})$$O(nf(p)) -time algorithm for the hybridization distance and the rSPr distance into $$O(n^{g(k)})$$O(nk) -time algorithms, where g is a computable function, and that the cluster reduction can be applied also to the TBR distance.

the hybridization number, the rSPR and TBR distances between two phylogenies are fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum level of any hybridization network displaying both trees, that is, by the minimum number of reticulations in any such network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fixed-parameter tractability of three important and related measures in phylogenetic tree comparison.
the fixed-parameter tractability of the three phylogenetic distances, which are of great importance in phylogenetics.
improving the fixed-parameter tractability of the problems of computing the hybridization number, the rSPR and the TBR distances between two phylogenies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all three measures are fixed-parameter tractable with respect to k.

all these problems are fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the natural parameter, and that the use of cluster reductions allows to transform any algorithm for any of them into an $$O(k \cdot n)O(k⋅n)$$ algorithm, where n is again the number of leaves, and k is a parameter that is much smaller (that is, more informative) than the natural parameter.
the problems of computing all three measures are fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the natural parameters, but also fixed- parameter tractable with respect a much stronger parameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cluster reduction rule allows us to reduce the parameter from the hybridization number or rSPR/TB distance to the minimum level of the phylogenies.

the cluster reduction rule is a general tool to transform algorithms for these problems from being fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the natural parameter into being fixed-parameter tractability with respect to the much smaller level parameter.
the hybridization number, the rSPR and TBR distances can be computed in $$O(f(k)\cdot n)$$ time for any fixed k.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in practice, the cluster reduction rule is likely to lead to a much better running time than the best known algorithms for these problems.
for all these problems, the use of cluster reductions can be used to transform a parameterization by the natural parameter into one by the level.
, in order to solve the problems mentioned above, it suffices to compute the minimum level of the phylogenies, and then to use this information as the parameter for the algorithm.
